detail: BanknoteNews states that, according to a ToloNews article of 6 January 2020, Da Afghanistan Bank awarded the Polish Security Printing Works (PWPW) a contract for new notes in 10, 20, 50 and 100 afghani denominations, and that on 1 February 2021 the Polish embassy in New Delhi announced that PWPW had delivered to Afghanistan 380 million newly printed banknotes. No contract value and no statement of an ongoing arrangement is given.

Tunisie Numerique lists Saudi Arabia among the Arab countries that print their banknotes domestically, naming the printing works as the 'Saudi Central Bank Printing Works' and describing it as giving the kingdom 'forte souverainete monetaire'. The article gives no founding date, location or production figures.
source_title: Quels sont les pays arabes qui impriment leur propre monnaie ?

detail: Tunisie Numerique lists Algeria among the Arab countries that print their banknotes domestically, stating 'La Banque d'Algerie imprime ses billets localement'. The article names no separate printing company and gives no location or volumes for the works.
source_title: Quels sont les pays arabes qui impriment leur propre monnaie ?

entity: Central Bank of Jordan national banknote printing facility
detail: Tunisie Numerique lists Jordan among the Arab countries that print their banknotes domestically, stating 'La Central Bank of Jordan possede une imprimerie nationale pour les billets'. The article gives the facility no separate corporate name and no location or volumes.
source_title: Quels sont les pays arabes qui impriment leur propre monnaie ?

detail: El Mostrador reports that Venezuela turned to the Russian state-owned money-printing company Goznak to print its banknotes, under a contract between Goznak and the Banco Central de Venezuela signed in November (on the article's account, November 2019). The article states nothing about Venezuela's own Casa de la Moneda and gives no contract value or volume.
source_title: Venezuela recurre a firma rusa para que imprima sus billetes

entity: China Banknote Printing and Minting Corporation
detail: Wikipedia describes the China Banknote Printing and Minting Corporation as a state-owned corporation headquartered in Beijing's Xicheng District that 'carries out the minting of all renminbi coins and printing of renminbi banknotes for the People's Republic of China', and as a public-sector agency within the People's Bank of China that bases currency production on the PBOC's macroeconomic planning. Only Wikipedia was found for this.
source_title: China Banknote Printing and Minting Corporation

detail: Wikipedia states that Goznak 'not only prints Russian money, but also prints banknotes of foreign countries', that it is 100% owned by the federal government with the Ministry of Finance as its parent, and that its branches include the Perm Printing Factory and Moscow printing factories; its head office is at 17 Mytnaya Street, Moscow. The page does not name the Bank of Russia as the customer for banknotes, and does not say which branch prints them. Only Wikipedia was found for this.

The Central Bank of Iceland's own announcement of the new 10,000 krona banknote states: 'The new notes were printed by De La Rue Plc. in the UK.' The statement covers that denomination only; the announcement says nothing about who prints Iceland's other notes.

A Reserve Bank of Fiji press release states that the bank 'signed an agreement for the printing of a series of new design Fiji banknotes with De La Rue International Limited' of the United Kingdom, and that a $100 note would be introduced for the first time. The release does not list the other denominations or the contract value.
source_title: Press Release No. 01/2006 - Printing of Fiji's New Currency Notes

detail: Securamonde reports on the Central Bank of Seychelles' new banknote family and states that the banknotes were 'printed by UK banknote printers De La Rue'. No contract value, volume or term is given.
